title: Quarterly roadmap: Hosted API model gating, onboarding & rollout plan
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures the quarterly roadmap planning for Hosted API + Model Catalog focused on establishing a reproducible model-gating pipeline, onboarding criteria, and a safe/staged rollout process for new model variants (including quantized variants). Goal is to reduce time-to-ship validated models from discovery -> hosted by 40% while keeping customer-facing regressions < 0.5% for quality metrics.

Objectives / OKRs (Q2):
- O1 (Adoption): Reduce model onboarding cycle time from PR -> hosted by 40%.
- O2 (Quality): Prevent quality regressions: median eval delta across target prompts < 0.5%.
- O3 (Reliability): New model variants must meet latency SLOs 99th <= 1.5x baseline for 95% of requests.
- O4 (Cost): Provide quantization guidance to reduce hosted per-token cost by 15% for compatible workloads.

Success metrics (how we measure):
- Time from model submission to gated approval (days). Target: median <= 7 days.
- Eval regression rate: percent of prompt suites with >1% regression. Target: <0.5%.
- Latency impact: delta p95 and p99 vs baseline. Target: p95 < +10% token latency.
- Customer incidents attributed to new model variants (count). Target: 0 for first 30 days.
- Model usage ramp (tokens/day) in first 4 weeks after general availability.

High-level milestones & timeline (Q2 weeks):
- Week 1 (Mar 30 - Apr 3): Finalize gating criteria doc and canonical eval suites (owner: Product). Create Confluence: /d/hosted-model-gating.
- Week 2: Implement automated eval job definitions in CI and link artifact storage (owner: Eng infra).
- Week 3: Define safety and privacy checklist (SRE/Security review) and sample audit logs for Private/Dedicated customers.
- Week 4: Run pilot onboarding for two candidate models (one open LLM, one distilled/quantized). Capture perf and quality metrics.
- Week 6: Design review & rollout plan sign-off (Design + PM + Eng).
- Week 8: Canary rollout to 5% traffic with automatic fallback policy. Observability hooks and regression alerts enabled.
- Week 12: Full GA if metrics pass, otherwise rollback and remediation.

Gating criteria (minimum to pass):
- Perf: p50/p95/p99 baseline comparisons recorded; no more than 20% p99 degradation for token-limited workloads without mitigation.
- Cost: cost-per-token estimate provided with quantization variant if available.
- Quality: pass canonical eval suites with <0.5% regression vs pinned reference model across primary prompt sets.
- Safety: safety scan run and manual review for high-risk categories; no unresolved high-priority safety flags.
- Observability: tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and rollout metrics dashboards created.
- Infra readiness: model variant supports KV cache/continuous batching in the runtime or has documented fallback behavior.

Rollout plan (hosted API):
- Stage 0: Internal validation (dev team only).
- Stage 1: Canary (5% traffic, automatic fallback to baseline if regression alerts fire).
- Stage 2: Gradual ramp to 25% over 72h if no alerts.
- Stage 3: 50%/75%/100% daily increases with post-mortem after 72h at each step.
- Safety net: immediate traffic cutover policy if customer-impact metric breach or increased error rate.

Cross-team responsibilities: 
- Product (Maya/Aidan): define OKRs, prioritize candidate models, liaise with customers for beta access.
- Eng (Serving/runtime): implement gating CI, performance benchmarks, rollout automation, and fallback.
- Eng (Infra/Observability): dashboards, tracer instrumentation, cost breakdown.
- Design: update Hosted API docs, create rollout copy and customer comm templates.
- Security & Compliance: KMS/audit checklist for Private/Dedicated onboarding.

Dependencies: must coordinate with Dedicated team for reserved capacity plan if initial canary traffic needs reserved GPU pools. See dependency list below.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Model passes offline evals but fails in tail production prompts. Mitigation: expand prompt coverage during pilot, enable fast rollback and shadow testing.
- Risk: Quantized variant increases hallucination rate. Mitigation: require secondary quality evals focused on factuality and regression thresholds locked.
- Risk: Infra capacity shortage during ramp. Mitigation: pre-book Dedicated burst capacity and prepare routing policy to fallback to cheaper variants.

Acceptance criteria (for GA):
- All gating criteria satisfied and documented.
- Canary ran 72h without triggering customer-impact alerts or unacceptable regressions.
- Release notes, runbooks, rollback steps, and customer communication templates posted.

Artifacts & links (to be created/updated):
- Confluence: /d/hosted-model-gating (draft created).
- GH: PRs for CI eval jobs (link to be added).
- Dashboards: hosted/model-gating/evals (placeholder).
- Design spec: Drive: Hosted API model selector UX mockups.

Notes on scope & trade-offs:
- We will not attempt full automated certification for every open model this quarter; focus on building the pipeline and gating a small set of high-impact models.
- Trade-off: stricter gating shortens risk but increases manual review workload. We'll invest in automation for evaluation and triage to reduce reviewer time.

Stakeholders & approvers:
- Approver (Product): Maya Chen
- Eng lead (runtime): Priya Nambiar
- Observability lead: Luis Alvarez
- Security reviewer: Hannah Schultz

Next steps / Action items (owner):
- PM: finalize gating doc and list candidate models by 2026-03-08 (Maya).
- Eng runtime: prototype CI runner for evals by 2026-03-15 (Aidan).
- Observability: draft dashboards for canary metrics by 2026-03-18 (Luis).
- Design: provide docs and notice templates by 2026-03-22 (Design).

Customer communication plan:
- Private beta invites for selected customers with explicit opt-in and SLA notes.
- Post-GA: update Hosted API catalog with model badges (stable/canary/quantized) and per-model performance summary.

Longer-term: Integrate gating pipeline with Model Lifecycle to enable automated re-eval on dataset drift and scheduled re-certification every quarter.
